correctness.rationale: The binary threshold argument is correct. Clipping a tree similarity to \([0,b]\) and integrating its threshold equivalence relations gives the lower bound \(\operatorname{Tree}(s)\ge b\operatorname{Clust}(A)\); a one-level tree built from any finite-core clustering gives the reverse inequality. Binary hyperbolicity is exactly the oriented bad-triangle probability. The Poisson-pivot estimates sum to \(3\lambda\beta+1/(e\lambda)\), whose optimization gives \(2\sqrt{3/e}\sqrt\beta\). The graph normalizations \(\operatorname{Clust}=2k/n^2\) and \(\beta=2p_3/n^3\) yield the stated \(e/6\) inequality, and the disjoint-\(K_{q,q}\) family confirms quadratic-order sharpness.
residual_risks: The theorem is restricted to reflexive two-valued similarities and finite-core clusterings exactly as stated.
